NDT training in Nevada: how it works for Nevada employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Nevada employers and technicians in Reno-Sparks, Las Vegas, Elko and the rural mining counties. Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET are delivered live online or onsite at your facility, mine or plant under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you against its written practice after training, logged experience, exams and a vision test. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Nevada.

Nevada's NDT market looks different from the Gulf Coast or the Midwest. There is almost no oil refining and no commercial nuclear power, but there are three large and growing drivers: battery and advanced manufacturing along the I-80 corridor east of Reno, the largest gold-mining complex in the United States plus a new generation of lithium projects in the north, and a construction, defence and infrastructure economy centred on Las Vegas. Each of those sectors inspects different things to different codes, and each has its own reasons for not wanting to send people out of state for weeks of classroom time. Online theory and onsite practicals solve that. This section sets out the courses, the certification path, the delivery options and the local regulatory context for radiography.

If you already know what you need, request a Nevada training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Nevada

Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, so the outlines and examinations can be adopted directly into your written practice. Worked examples reflect Nevada work: battery-plant structures and process piping, mill and processing-plant equipment at mines, crushers and heavy mobile equipment, autoclaves and pressure vessels, geothermal and gas-fired power plant piping, structural steel on resort and stadium construction, pipeline welds and aircraft components.

MethodLevelsWhat Nevada employers use it forPrerequisite

Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline and plant piping welds, castings, pressure-vessel seamsNone for Level I; radiation safety training and state requirements for field work

Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, IIStainless and non-ferrous process equipment, aerospace parts, castingsNone for Level I

Ultrasonic testing. UT Level I covers wave propagation, transducers, couplants, reference standards, straight-beam and angle-beam technique and thickness gauging. Level II adds DAC and TCG construction, flaw location and sizing, and interpretation against code criteria. In Nevada, corrosion and erosion monitoring on slurry and process piping at mines, thickness surveys on tanks and vessels, and structural weld inspection on Las Vegas construction are the core applications.

PAUT and TOFD. Taught at Level II, these cover focal laws, sectorial and linear scanning, encoded data, TOFD geometry, analysis and reporting. They are valuable to Nevada contractors because radiography on a live construction site or inside a busy manufacturing plant forces exclusion zones and stops other work, while encoded UT does not.

Radiographic testing. RT covers radiation physics, isotope and X-ray sources, film and digital detectors, exposure calculation, image quality indicators and interpretation. Nevada is an NRC Agreement State, so field radiography requires a state licence and qualified radiographers, covered in the regulator section below.

MT, PT and VT. These are the workhorse methods of the Nevada mining industry, where haul-truck frames, shovel booms, crusher components and mill shells are inspected on a maintenance cycle. MT covers yoke, prod and coil technique and fluorescent wet method; PT covers visible and fluorescent systems; VT covers direct and remote visual examination and code acceptance criteria.

Eddy current. ET covers impedance-plane analysis, surface probes, bolt-hole inspection, bobbin-probe tube testing and conductivity. Nevada demand comes from power and geothermal plant heat-exchanger tubing and from military and civil aviation maintenance.

Level III preparation. Senior technicians can prepare for the ASNT Level III Basic and method examinations through ASNT Level III training, including procedure writing and running an employer certification programme.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Nevada, step by step

Nevada does not issue a state NDT licence. Certification under SNT-TC-1A is granted by your employer against its written practice. The route is:

  1. Employer written practice defining methods, levels, training and experience requirements, exam content, grading and recertification.
  2. Classroom training for the method and level, to the hours in the written practice. See the training requirements matrix for current figures.
  3. On-the-job experience under supervision, logged and verifiable. Training hours and experience hours are both required.
  4. General examination on the theory of the method.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens with known discontinuities, administered and graded under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, near vision annually.
  8. Certification issued and signed by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the written-practice interval, by examination or evidence of continuing performance where permitted.

More detail is in our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Nevada crews

Nevada's industrial sites are far apart: the mines around Elko, Carlin and Battle Mountain are hours from Reno, and Las Vegas is a full day's drive from both. Delivery is built around that geography:

  • Live online classroom. Instructor-led theory that technicians can join from a mine camp, a Sparks plant or a Las Vegas office. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility or site. The instructor comes to your plant, mine maintenance shop or fabrication yard, trains on your equipment and specimens, and can administer examinations under Level III oversight. Onsite training at mine sites is arranged around your site access and safety induction requirements; MSHA site training remains the operator's responsibility.
  • Blended. Theory online first, followed by a short onsite practical block that fits rotating rosters.

We plan around your calendar: mill and processing-plant shutdowns, power and geothermal plant outages, manufacturing line changeovers and construction milestones. Many mining crews work fixed rotations, so training can be split across rotations rather than pulling people off shift. Ask about onsite training for your Nevada crew, or see corporate NDT training for multi-site programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Nevada

  • Battery and advanced manufacturing. The Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center in Storey County hosts the Tesla Gigafactory and Panasonic's battery operations, and battery-materials recycling and processing companies have grown up nearby. Plant structures, process piping, pressure systems and production equipment are inspected with VT, UT, MT and PT, largely under AWS D1.1 and ASME B31.3 practice.
  • Gold, silver and lithium mining. Nevada Gold Mines, the Barrick and Newmont joint venture, operates complexes around Carlin, Cortez and Turquoise Ridge, and other producers operate across the state. Lithium development at Thacker Pass adds a new processing plant. Mining NDT covers mobile equipment frames and components, crushers, mills, conveyors, leach and processing tanks, autoclaves, pressure vessels and slurry piping. MSHA governs site safety; inspection codes vary by equipment and owner.
  • Construction and structural steel. Las Vegas resort, stadium and high-rise construction, and industrial buildings in Reno-Sparks, require structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1, usually under special inspection programmes administered by local building departments. VT and UT dominate; clients often also require an AWS CWI, which Atlantis does not train.
  • Power generation. Gas-fired plants operated by NV Energy and others, a substantial geothermal fleet in northern Nevada, and the Hoover Dam hydroelectric plant on the Arizona border create boiler, piping, turbine and heat-exchanger inspection work under ASME Section I and B31.1.
  • Pipelines and fuel. Interstate gas transmission lines, including the Kern River system serving Las Vegas, and the refined-products pipeline supplying southern Nevada bring API 1104 weld inspection and integrity work under PHMSA rules.
  • Aerospace and defence. Nellis and Creech Air Force Bases near Las Vegas, Naval Air Station Fallon, and aerospace companies in the Reno-Sparks area generate ET, PT and UT work on aircraft and components. Military and aerospace programmes often specify NAS 410 or technical orders; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based.
  • Federal research sites. The Nevada National Security Site north of Las Vegas operates under DOE and NNSA requirements, with its own qualification and security clearance rules.

Radiography licensing in Nevada. Nevada is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials licences, including industrial radiography, are administered by the Radiation Control Program within the Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health, which also registers X-ray equipment. A company performing field radiography needs a state licence with an approved radiation safety programme and radiation safety officer; radiographers need radiation safety training and a qualifying radiographer certification, and must follow two-person, surveying and dosimetry rules at temporary job sites. Work on federal enclaves such as military bases or DOE sites can fall under NRC or DOE jurisdiction rather than the state, so check jurisdiction with the site before mobilising. Atlantis RT courses cover interpretation competence; licensing and dosimetry remain with the employer.

What Nevada employers ask for. Common requirements are ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, MT and VT; PT for stainless and aerospace work; RT Level II plus radiographer credentials for field radiography; conventional UT before PAUT; and, on structural projects, a CWI on the team. Some employers with international owners also ask for ISO 9712 certification, which is a separate third-party scheme; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Level III services and written practices for Nevada NDT companies

Nevada's fast-growing manufacturing and mining sectors include many operations that do their own NDT without a resident Level III. Under SNT-TC-1A somebody must still own the written practice, approve procedures and administer exams. Atlantis provides that as an outsourced service:

  • Written practice development and gap reviews against the current SNT-TC-1A edition; see written practice development.
  • Procedures and techniques for the equipment and codes you inspect to, from mobile mining equipment to AWS D1.1 structural steel and ASME pressure equipment.
  • Examinations prepared, administered and graded under Level III authority, with records kept for audit.
  • Audit and supplier-qualification support for customer audits, owner pre-qualification and ISO 9001 surveillance.

Read our SNT-TC-1A guidance for the rules, then book a Level III consultation to discuss your programme.

Practise before the practical exam

For technicians on remote rotations, Practical NDT offers a way to rehearse between sessions. The 3D simulator covers 12 NDT methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Trainees can repeat set-ups, scan patterns and indication recognition as often as they need.

It is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A must be performed on real specimens and graded under Level III authority. For written-exam revision, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Atlantis training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop authors the course material, provides Level III oversight of examinations and works directly with Nevada employers on written practices and programme planning.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Nevada

How do I get NDT certified in Nevada?

There is no state NDT licence. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after classroom training, supervised experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. Level I training in UT, MT or VT is a practical first step toward trainee roles with manufacturers, mines and inspection contractors.

Can I take NDT training online in Nevada?

Yes. Classroom theory is available live online anywhere in Nevada, including mine sites with a reliable connection. The practical training and practical exam must be done on real equipment and specimens, normally onsite at your employer. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and your prior training and experience. SNT-TC-1A sets recommended minimum classroom and experience hours; see the training requirements matrix. Send us your hours and we will map what remains.

Do I need a license for radiography in Nevada?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence or X-ray registration from the Nevada Radiation Control Program, as Nevada is an NRC Agreement State. Individual radiographers need radiation safety training and a qualifying radiographer certification and work under the licensee's programme. Work on federal sites may fall under a different jurisdiction.

What does NDT training cost in Nevada?

Quote on request. The price depends on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, site travel and whether examinations and Level III services are included. Quotes come back within one business day: request a Nevada quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Nevada employers?

Yes. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for US industrial employers, including manufacturers, mines, construction contractors and inspection companies in Nevada. Certification is employer-specific, so a new employer may re-examine you before certifying you under its own written practice.

Do mining companies in Nevada hire NDT technicians?

Yes. Mines and their maintenance contractors inspect mobile equipment, crushers, mills, tanks, vessels and piping, mostly with MT, UT, VT and PT. Site roles also require MSHA safety training, which the operator provides separately.

Which NDT method is most useful in Las Vegas?

On construction, VT and UT on structural welds are the most requested, often alongside a CWI. MT is used on structural and equipment welds, and PAUT is growing where contractors want to avoid radiography exclusion zones on busy sites.

Can you train our team at the Reno-Sparks industrial centre?

Yes. Onsite training at your facility is the usual approach for groups, using your equipment and specimens, with examinations under Level III oversight arranged around production schedules.

Can a Nevada company certify its own technicians?

Yes, with a compliant written practice and a qualified Level III to administer and sign. Many companies use an outsourced Level III; see written practice development.

Does Atlantis offer ISO 9712 or aerospace NAS 410 certification?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Nevada employers ask for ISO 9712 or NAS 410, and our method training builds the knowledge those schemes assume, but the certification itself must come through those schemes.

What do NDT technicians earn in Nevada?

Pay varies widely between mining rotations, construction and manufacturing. For sourced ranges, see the NDT salary guide 2026.
